hindi: अब इसके बाद हम अष्टौनिन्दितीय अध्याय की व्याख्या करेंगे।
english: Now, therefore, we shall expound the chapter on the eight censured persons (Aṣṭauninditīya).
notes: Prose opening formula of the chapter; the unit is typed as a verse in the input but is a prose line. Aṣṭauninditīya is a derived chapter name in -īya and is not split into members.

hindi: ऐसा भगवान् आत्रेय ने कहा।
english: Thus said the venerable Ātreya.
notes: Prose formula; ha and sma are particles, not rendered separately.

hindi: यहाँ शरीर को लेकर आठ पुरुष निन्दित होते हैं; जैसे — अत्यन्त लम्बा, अत्यन्त नाटा, अत्यधिक रोमों वाला, रोमरहित, अत्यन्त काला, अत्यन्त गोरा, अत्यन्त स्थूल और अत्यन्त कृश।
english: Here, with regard to the body, eight persons are censured, namely: the excessively tall, the excessively short, the excessively hairy, the hairless, the excessively dark, the excessively fair, the excessively obese and the excessively lean.
notes: Prose line typed as a verse unit. The commas and semicolon attached to tokens are left out of the words.
lines_deva: इह खलु शरीरमधिकृत्याष्टौ पुरुषा निन्दिता भवन्ति; तद्यथा --- अतिदीर्घश्च, अतिह्रस्वश्च, अतिलोमा च, अलोमा च, अतिकृष्णश्च, अतिगौरश्च, अतिस्थूलश्च, अतिकृशश्चेति
lines_iast: iha khalu śarīramadhikṛtyāṣṭau puruṣā ninditā bhavanti; tadyathā --- atidīrghaśca, atihrasvaśca, atilomā ca, alomā ca, atikṛṣṇaśca, atigauraśca, atisthūlaśca, atikṛśaśceti

words.gloss: in the excessively obese and the excessively lean

hindi: उनमें अत्यन्त स्थूल और अत्यन्त कृश में इसके अतिरिक्त और दूसरे विशेष निन्दनीय बातें होती हैं।
english: Among them, in the excessively obese and the excessively lean there are, further, other special censurable features.
notes: atisthūlakṛśayoḥ may be locative or genitive dual (both -yoḥ); taken as locative ('in'). bhūya eva: 'still more, further'.

hindi: अत्यन्त स्थूल पुरुष के ये आठ दोष होते हैं — आयु का ह्रास, गति का अवरोध, मैथुन में कठिनाई, दुर्बलता, दुर्गन्ध, स्वेद से कष्ट, अत्यधिक भूख और अत्यधिक प्यास।
english: Of the excessively obese, first, there are these eight defects (doṣa): shortening of life-span, impediment of speed, difficulty in sexual intercourse, weakness, bad odour, trouble from sweat, excessive hunger and excessive thirst.

text_flags.why: possible typo: the same list in unit P3 reads singular pipāsātiyogaś, and every other item of the list is singular

notes: doṣa here means the eight defects, not the bodily doṣas. kṛcchravyavāyatā: 'the state of having difficult intercourse'. If the plural pipāsātiyogāḥ is kept, the sense is unchanged.
lines_deva: अतिस्थूलस्य तावदायुषो ह्रासो जवोपरोधः कृच्छ्रव्यवायता दौर्बल्यं दौर्गन्ध्यं स्वेदाबाधः क्षुदतिमात्रं पिपासातियोगाश्चेति भवन्त्यष्टौ दोषाः
lines_iast: atisthūlasya tāvadāyuṣo hrāso javoparodhaḥ kṛcchravyavāyatā daurbalyaṃ daurgandhyaṃ svedābādhaḥ kṣudatimātraṃ pipāsātiyogāśceti bhavantyaṣṭau doṣāḥ

words.gloss: from the use of heavy, sweet, cold and unctuous things
words.gram: m. abl. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

words.gloss: from the nature of the seed

hindi: वह अत्यन्त स्थूलता अत्यधिक पेट भरने से, गुरु, मधुर, शीत और स्निग्ध पदार्थों के सेवन से, व्यायाम न करने से, मैथुन न करने से, दिन में सोने से, सदा प्रसन्न रहने से, चिन्तन न करने से और बीज के स्वभाव से उत्पन्न होती है।
english: That excessive obesity arises from over-filling, from the use of heavy, sweet, cold and unctuous things, from lack of exercise, from lack of sexual intercourse, from day-sleep, from constant cheerfulness, from absence of mental exertion, and from the nature of the seed.

text_flags.why: 'sngidha' is not a word; letters transposed for snigdha 'unctuous'

notes: The whole prose line is a single printed token. bījasvabhāva 'the nature of the seed' is translated literally (inherited nature). acintana 'not thinking' may mean freedom from worry.

words.gloss: from having a sharp digestive fire
from having abundant Vāta in the bowel

hindi: क्योंकि उस अत्यधिक मेद वाले पुरुष में केवल मेद बढ़ता है, दूसरी धातुएँ वैसे नहीं बढ़तीं, इसलिए उसकी आयु का ह्रास होता है; मेद की शिथिलता, सुकुमारता और भारीपन से गति का अवरोध होता है; शुक्र की अल्पता से और मेद से मार्गों के ढके होने से मैथुन में कठिनाई होती है; धातुओं की असमानता से दुर्बलता; मेद के दोष से, मेद के स्वभाव से और स्वेद उत्पन्न करने के कारण दुर्गन्ध; मेद का श्लेष्मा से संसर्ग होने, उसके स्रवणशील होने, उसकी अधिकता, उसके भारीपन और उसके व्यायाम न सह सकने से स्वेद से कष्ट; तथा तीक्ष्ण अग्नि होने से और कोष्ठ में प्रचुर वायु होने से अत्यधिक भूख और अत्यधिक प्यास होती है।
english: For in him, the excessively fat person, fat alone accumulates, not the other dhātus likewise; therefore his life-span is shortened. From the looseness, delicacy and heaviness of fat there is impediment of speed; from scantiness of semen (śukra) and from his pathways being covered by fat there is difficulty in sexual intercourse; weakness, from the imbalance of the dhātus; bad odour, from the defect of fat, from the nature of fat and from its producing sweat; trouble from sweat, from the association of fat with Kapha (śleṣman), its oozing nature, its abundance, its heaviness and its inability to bear exercise; and excessive hunger and excessive thirst, from a sharp digestive fire (agni) and abundant Vāta (vāyu) in the bowel (koṣṭha).
notes: Prose explanation of the eight defects of P1. 'na tathetare dhātavaḥ': the verb upacīyante is understood. viṣyanditva: vi-√syand 'ooze' (ṣ by rule after vi). medasaḥ (token 21) is taken with all the following ablatives up to vyāyāmāsahatvāt. The ablatives govern the nominatives that follow or precede them, as the punctuation shows.
lines_deva: तस्य ह्यतिमात्रमेदस्विनो मेद एवोपचीयते न तथेतरे धातवः, तस्मादस्यायुषो ह्रासः; शैथिल्यात् सौकुमार्याद्गुरुत्वाच्च मेदसो जवोपरोधः, शुक्राबहुत्वान्मेदसावृतमार्गत्वाच्च कृच्छ्रव्यवायता, दौर्बल्यमसमत्वाद्धातूनां, दौर्गन्ध्यं मेदोदोषान्मेदसः स्वभावात् स्वेदनत्वाच्च, मेदसः श्लेष्मसंसर्गाद्विष्यन्दित्वाद्बहुत्वाद्गुरुत्वाद्व्यायामासहत्वाच्च स्वेदाबाधः, तीक्ष्णाग्नित्वात् प्रभूतकोष्ठवायुत्वाच्च क्षुदतिमात्रं पिपासातियोगश्चेति
lines_iast: tasya hyatimātramedasvino meda evopacīyate na tathetare dhātavaḥ, tasmādasyāyuṣo hrāsaḥ; śaithilyāt saukumāryādgurutvācca medaso javoparodhaḥ, śukrābahutvānmedasāvṛtamārgatvācca kṛcchravyavāyatā, daurbalyamasamatvāddhātūnāṃ, daurgandhyaṃ medodoṣānmedasaḥ svabhāvāt svedanatvācca, medasaḥ śleṣmasaṃsargādviṣyanditvādbahutvādgurutvādvyāyāmāsahatvācca svedābādhaḥ, tīkṣṇāgnitvāt prabhūtakoṣṭhavāyutvācca kṣudatimātraṃ pipāsātiyogaśceti

hindi: और यहाँ ये श्लोक हैं: मेद से मार्गों के ढके होने के कारण वायु विशेष रूप से कोष्ठ में विचरता हुआ अग्नि को प्रदीप्त करता है और आहार को सुखा भी देता है।
english: And here there are: Because its pathways are covered by fat, Vāta (vāyu), moving especially in the bowel (koṣṭha), kindles the digestive fire (agni) and also dries up the food.
notes: The lead-in bhavanti cātra is printed as the first line of the unit. viśeṣataḥ may go with koṣṭhe ('especially in the bowel') or with caran; either way the sense is the same.

hindi: इसलिए वह आहार को शीघ्र पचा लेता है और भोजन की अत्यधिक इच्छा करता है, तथा समय का अतिक्रमण होने पर कुछ घोर विकारों को प्राप्त होता है।
english: Therefore he digests food quickly and craves it excessively, and, when the time is transgressed, he incurs some terrible disorders.
notes: saḥ is taken as the obese man (subject of atikāṅkṣati and aśnute). kālavyatikramāt: the time is understood as the time of eating; the text does not say so explicitly.

hindi: ये दोनों, अग्नि और मारुत, विशेष रूप से उपद्रव उत्पन्न करने वाले हैं; क्योंकि ये दोनों स्थूल पुरुष को उसी प्रकार जला देते हैं जैसे दावानल वन को।
english: These two, fire (agni) and Vāta (māruta), especially cause complications; for these two burn the obese one as a forest fire burns the forest.

text_flags.why: possible: dahataḥ needs an accusative object and sthūlā has no fitting case; a lost final nasal gives sthūlaṃ (acc. sg., used in words) or sthūlān (acc. pl.); both keep the metre
possible: the simile needs an accusative 'forest'; vanā is not a classical acc. form; a lost anusvāra (as in sthūlā) gives vanaṃ with the same metre

notes: If the printed forms are kept, sthūlā(n) ... vanā(ni) would be read as plurals 'the obese ... forests'; the sense is the same. upadrava = complication (उपद्रव).
lines_deva: एतौ हि दहतः स्थूला वनदावो वना यथा
lines_iast: etau hi dahataḥ sthūlā vanadāvo vanā yathā

words.gram: n. loc. sg., ppp. sam-√vṛdh (loc. abs.)

hindi: जब मेद अत्यधिक बढ़ जाता है, तब अनिल आदि सहसा ही दारुण विकार उत्पन्न करके शीघ्र जीवन को नष्ट कर देते हैं।
english: When fat has increased greatly, Vāta (anila) and the others suddenly produce dreadful disorders and quickly destroy life.

text_flags.why: medasi + atīva gives medasyatīva; the printed form has lost the a, and the line is then one syllable short of 8

notes: anilādayaḥ: 'anila and the rest'; the others are understood as the other doṣas.

words.gloss: from excessive increase of fat and flesh
words.gram: n. abl. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

words.gloss: with pendulous buttocks, belly and breasts
whose energy does not match his bulk

hindi: मेद और मांस की अत्यधिक वृद्धि से जिसके नितम्ब, पेट और स्तन लटकते हों और जिसका उत्साह उसकी वृद्धि के अनुरूप न हो, वह मनुष्य अत्यन्त स्थूल कहलाता है।
english: A man who, from excessive increase of fat and flesh, has pendulous buttocks, belly and breasts, and whose energy does not match his growth, is called excessively obese.
notes: sphig- = sphij 'buttock' (j becomes g before u). ayathopacayotsāhaḥ: 'having energy not in proportion to (his) growth'.

hindi: इस प्रकार मेदस्वी पुरुष के दोष, कारण और रूप बता दिए गए; अब इसके बाद अत्यन्त कृशता के विषय में जो कहना है, वह कहा जाएगा।
english: Thus the defects (doṣa), causes and symptoms (rūpa) of the fat person have been stated; after this, what is to be said about extreme leanness will be stated.
notes: nirdiṣṭam (n. sg.) sums up the three items. rūpa = symptoms (form).
lines_deva: इति मेदस्विनो दोषा हेतवो रूपमेव च
lines_iast: iti medasvino doṣā hetavo rūpameva ca

words.gram: n. gen. pl., karmadhāraya (dvandva second part)

words.gloss: suppression of urges and of sleep
words.gram: m. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: रूक्ष अन्न-पान का सेवन, लङ्घन, अल्प भोजन, क्रियाओं का अतियोग, शोक और वेग तथा निद्रा को रोकना,
english: The use of dry food and drink, lightening (laṅghana), scanty eating, excessive use of procedures (kriyā), grief, suppression of urges (vega) and of sleep,

text_flags.why: possible: 'pramitya' is not a fitting form; pramita 'measured, scanty' + aśana gives pramitāśanam with the same syllable count

notes: The sentence continues into unit 12, whose verb kurvanti governs this list. kriyā is taken as therapeutic procedures; the text does not specify which.

hindi: रूक्ष द्रव्य से उद्वर्तन, स्नान का अभ्यास, प्रकृति, बुढ़ापा, विकार का बने रहना और क्रोध — ये मनुष्य को अत्यन्त कृश कर देते हैं।
english: rubbing (udvartana) with dry substance, habitual bathing, constitution (prakṛti), old age, lingering of disorders, and anger make a man very lean.

text_flags.why: 'kruvanti' is not a form; letters transposed for kurvanti 'they make', the verb the list of units 11-12 needs

notes: rūkṣasyodvartanam may also be read 'rubbing of a dry (person)'; taken as rubbing with a dry substance. vikārānuśaya: anuśaya 'remaining after, lingering'; taken as the persistence of disease. prakṛti here is the natural constitution.

words.gloss: excessive cold, heat and sexual intercourse

hindi: कृश पुरुष व्यायाम, अति-सौहित्य, भूख, प्यास, रोग और औषध को नहीं सह पाता; उसी प्रकार अत्यधिक शीत, उष्णता और मैथुन को नहीं सह पाता।
english: The lean man does not tolerate exercise, over-satiety (sauhitya), hunger, thirst, disease and medicine; likewise excessive cold, heat and sexual intercourse.
notes: ati- in atiśītoṣṇamaithunam may govern only śīta or all three members; taken with all three.

hindi: प्लीहा, कास, क्षय, श्वास, गुल्म, अर्श, उदर रोग और ग्रहणी में स्थित रोग प्रायः कृश पुरुष पर आक्रमण करते हैं।
english: Plīhā (spleen disease), cough (kāsa), wasting (kṣaya), dyspnoea (śvāsa), gulma, arśas, udara diseases and the diseases located in the grahaṇī mostly assail the lean man.
notes: plīhā (from plīhan, the spleen) names a disease of the spleen here. Disease names are kept in Sanskrit as in the glossary.
lines_deva: प्लीहा कासः क्षयः श्वासो गुल्मोऽर्शांस्युदराणि च
lines_iast: plīhā kāsaḥ kṣayaḥ śvāso gulmo'rśāṃsyudarāṇi ca

words.gloss: with dried-up buttocks, belly and neck
covered with a network of vessels

hindi: जिसके नितम्ब, पेट और गर्दन सूखे हुए हों, जो धमनियों के जाल से व्याप्त हो, जिसमें त्वचा और हड्डियाँ शेष रह गई हों और जिसके पर्व स्थूल हों, वह मनुष्य अत्यन्त कृश माना गया है।
english: A man with dried-up buttocks, belly and neck, covered with a network of vessels (dhamanī), left with skin and bone, with prominent joints, is considered very lean.
notes: sthūlaparvan: 'having thick joints', i.e. joints that stand out. tvak here is human skin.

words.gloss: the excessively obese and the excessively lean

hindi: ये दोनों, अत्यन्त स्थूल और अत्यन्त कृश पुरुष, सदा रोगी रहते हैं, और इनकी सदा कर्शन तथा बृंहण उपायों से चिकित्सा करनी चाहिए।
english: These two men, the excessively obese and the excessively lean, are always diseased, and they are always to be treated with reducing (karśana) and nourishing (bṛṃhaṇa) measures.
notes: The text pairs karśana and bṛṃhaṇa with the two men without saying 'respectively'; the obese is the one to be reduced and the lean the one to be nourished (units 20 ff.). hi in line 2 is taken as an emphatic particle.

hindi: स्थूलता और कृशता में कृशता श्रेष्ठ है, क्योंकि वे दोनों समान उपकरण वाले हैं; यदि दोनों पर रोग आए, तो वह स्थूल को ही अधिक पीड़ित करेगा।
english: Between obesity and leanness, leanness is better, for the two are equal in means (upakaraṇa); if disease should come upon both, it is the obese one that it would afflict severely.
notes: sthaulyakārśye: a samāhāra dvandva (neuter singular), here in the locative 'between obesity and leanness'; it could also be read as a nominative dual ('of obesity and leanness, leanness is better'). samopakaraṇau 'having equal means' is unclear: it may mean that both are equally provided with the means (of treatment); taken literally.
lines_deva: स्थौल्यकार्श्ये वरं कार्श्यं समोपकरणौ हि तौ
lines_iast: sthaulyakārśye varaṃ kārśyaṃ samopakaraṇau hi tau

hindi: परन्तु जिस मनुष्य का मांस का प्रमाण सम हो, शरीर का संहनन सम हो और इन्द्रियाँ दृढ़ हों, वह विकारों के बल से पराजित नहीं होता।
english: But a man with a balanced measure of flesh and balanced compactness of body (saṃhanana), with firm senses, is not overcome by the force of disorders.

text_flags.why: possible: 'sāhanana' is not a known word; saṃhanana 'compactness of body' fits the sense and has the same syllable count

words.gram: m. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)
m. nom. sg., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: वह भूख, प्यास और धूप को सहने वाला, शीत और व्यायाम को सहने वाला, सम रूप से पचाने वाला, सम जरण वाला और सम मांस-संचय वाला माना गया है।
english: He is considered to endure hunger, thirst and sun, to endure cold and exercise, to digest evenly, to assimilate evenly and to have a balanced accumulation of flesh.

text_flags.why: the printed line has 7 syllables in the first quarter (one short of 8); -sahaḥ 'enduring' restores the metre and parallels saṃsahaḥ in the same line

notes: The subject is the man of unit 18. samajaraḥ: from √jṝ, whose causative jarayati 'digests' is used in unit 6; taken as even digestion; it could also come from jarā 'old age' ('ageing evenly'). samapaktā: paktṛ 'digester'.

hindi: स्थूलों के कर्शन के लिए जो गुरु और अतर्पण हो, वह इष्ट है; और कृशों के बृंहण के लिए जो लघु और सन्तर्पण हो, वह।
english: For reducing (karśana) the obese, what is heavy and non-replenishing (atarpaṇa) is desired; and for nourishing (bṛṃhaṇa) the lean, what is light and replenishing (saṃtarpaṇa).
notes: iṣṭam is understood again with the second line.
lines_deva: गुरु चातर्पणं चेष्टं स्थूलानां कर्शनं प्रति
कृशानां बृंहणार्थं च लघु संतर्पणं च यत्
lines_iast: guru cātarpaṇaṃ ceṣṭaṃ sthūlānāṃ karśanaṃ prati
kṛśānāṃ bṛṃhaṇārthaṃ ca laghu saṃtarpaṇaṃ ca yat

words.gram: n. nom. pl., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: वात को नष्ट करने वाले तथा श्लेष्मा और मेद को हरने वाले अन्न-पान, रूक्ष, उष्ण और तीक्ष्ण वस्तियाँ, तथा रूक्ष उद्वर्तन,
english: Vāta-destroying foods and drinks that also remove Kapha (śleṣman) and fat; dry, hot and sharp enemas (basti); and dry rubbings (udvartana);
notes: Units 21 to 24 continue the list of measures for the obese begun in unit 20; there is no new main verb. vasti is the printed spelling of basti 'enema'.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., vṛddhi derivative of triphalā (adj. with prayogaḥ)
m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: गुडूची और भद्रमुस्ता का प्रयोग, तथा त्रिफला का प्रयोग, तक्र और अरिष्ट के प्रयोग, तथा माक्षिक का प्रयोग,
english: the administration of guḍūcī and bhadramustā, likewise the administration of triphalā (traiphala), administrations of buttermilk (takra) and ariṣṭa, and the administration of mākṣika;
notes: takrāriṣṭa may also be one item, 'an ariṣṭa made with buttermilk'; taken as two (the plural prayogāḥ allows either). mākṣika is a kind of honey; the same word also names a mineral, so the reading is not certain. Identifications: guḍūcī = Tinospora cordifolia (standard); bhadramustā = Cyperus rotundus (probable).

words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: विडङ्ग, नागर, क्षार, काले लोह का चूर्ण, मधु, और यव तथा आमलक का चूर्ण — क्षौद्र के साथ प्रयोग,
english: viḍaṅga, dry ginger (nāgara), alkali (kṣāra), powder of black metal (kālaloha), honey (madhu), and powder of barley and āmalaka; administration combined with honey (kṣaudra);
notes: madhu and kṣaudra both mean honey: madhu is one item of the list and kṣaudra the vehicle of the administration. Identifications: viḍaṅga = Embelia ribes (standard); āmalaka = Phyllanthus emblica (standard). prayogaḥ kṣaudrasaṃyutaḥ may go with the barley-āmalaka powder alone or with the whole list; the text does not say.

words.gloss: of the five roots beginning with bilva
words.gram: n. gen. sg., tat-puruṣa with dvigu

hindi: बिल्व आदि पञ्चमूल का क्षौद्र के साथ प्रयोग, शिलाजतु का प्रयोग और अग्निमन्थ का उत्तम रस,
english: the administration of the five roots beginning with bilva (bilvādipañcamūla) combined with honey (kṣaudra), the administration of śilājatu, and the excellent juice of agnimantha;

text_flags.why: possible: ṣa- cannot begin a word here; either a stray letter (agnimantharasaḥ 'juice of agnimantha', used in words) or ṣ for s with lost length (sāgnimantharasaḥ 'with agnimantha juice', qualifying śilājatuprayogaḥ); both keep 8 syllables, so the reading is uncertain

notes: paraḥ may mean 'excellent' or 'further'. Identification: bilva = Aegle marmelos (standard). The reading of the last word is uncertain (see text_flags).

hindi: प्रशातिका, प्रियङ्गु, श्यामाक, यवक, यव, जूर्णाह्व, कोद्रव, मुद्ग, कुलत्थ, चक्रमुद्गक,
english: praśātikā, priyaṅgu, śyāmāka, yavaka, barley (yava), jūrṇāhva, kodrava, mudga, kulattha, cakramudgaka,
notes: A list of grains and pulses; the sentence continues into unit 26 (prayojyāni 'are to be used as food'). kulatthāścakramudgakāḥ is split kulatthāḥ + cakramudgakāḥ (without a 'ca'); the alternative kulatthāḥ ca + kramudgakāḥ gives no known word. Identifications: kodrava = Paspalum scrobiculatum (standard); mudga = green gram, Vigna radiata (standard); kulattha = horse gram, Macrotyloma uniflorum (standard). praśātikā, priyaṅgu (as a grain), yavaka, jūrṇāhva and cakramudgaka are left unidentified here.

hindi: और आढकी के बीज, पटोल और आमलक के साथ, भोजन के लिए प्रयोग करने चाहिए; और बाद में पीने के लिए मधु-जल।
english: and the seeds of āḍhakī, together with paṭola and āmalaka, are to be used as food; and, as a drink afterwards, honey-water.

text_flags.why: possible: 'jāḍhakī' is not a known word; āḍhakī (a pulse) fits the list of grains and pulses of unit 25 and keeps 8 syllables; the j may also be a typo for c (cāḍhakīnāṃ = ca āḍhakīnām)
possible: pānām has no fitting case; the n. nom. sg. pānaṃ 'drink' fits with madhūdakam and keeps the metre

notes: prayojyāni also governs the grains of unit 25. āḍhakī rests on the conjecture in text_flags. Identification: paṭola = Trichosanthes dioica (standard); āmalaka as in unit 23.

words.gram: m. acc. pl., upapada tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: और अनुपान के लिए मेद, मांस और कफ को दूर करने वाले अरिष्टों को, अत्यधिक स्थूलता के नाश के लिए, विभाग करके प्रयोग करे।
english: And for destroying excessive obesity one should apportion and administer, as after-drink (anupāna), ariṣṭas that remove fat, flesh and Kapha.
notes: saṃvibhajya 'having divided up': the text does not say by what (dose or time).

hindi: जो स्थूलता को छोड़ना चाहता है, वह जागरण, मैथुन, व्यायाम और चिन्तन को क्रम से बढ़ाए।
english: One who wishes to give up obesity should gradually increase wakefulness, sexual intercourse, exercise and mental exertion.
notes: cintanāni (pl.) 'thinkings', i.e. mental exertion or worry; the opposite of acintana in P2.
lines_deva: प्रजागरं व्यवायं च व्यायामं चिन्तनानि च
lines_iast: prajāgaraṃ vyavāyaṃ ca vyāyāmaṃ cintanāni ca

words.gloss: cessation of worry, intercourse and exercise
words.gram: m. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: निद्रा, हर्ष, सुखद शय्या, मन की निश्चिन्तता, शान्ति, चिन्ता, मैथुन और व्यायाम से विराम, प्रिय का दर्शन,
english: Sleep, joy, a comfortable bed, contentment of mind, calm, cessation of worry, sexual intercourse and exercise, the sight of what is dear,
notes: Begins the list of measures for the lean; the sentence continues beyond unit 30, so no verb is in this chunk. priyadarśana may also mean 'the sight of dear ones'.
lines_deva: स्वप्नो हर्षः सुखा शय्या मनसो निर्वृतिः शमः
lines_iast: svapno harṣaḥ sukhā śayyā manaso nirvṛtiḥ śamaḥ

hindi: नया अन्न, नया मद्य, ग्राम्य, आनूप और औदक प्राणियों के मांसरस, संस्कारित मांस, दही, घी और दूध,
english: new grains, new wine (madya), the meat-juices (rasa) of domestic, marsh and aquatic animals, prepared meats, curd, ghee (sarpis) and milk,

text_flags.why: payāṃsai is not a form; the n. nom. pl. of payas is payāṃsi, matching the other neuter plurals of the line

notes: rasāḥ with animal groups is taken as meat-juices; 'animals' is understood. The list continues beyond this chunk.
lines_deva: संस्कृतानि च मांसानि दधि सर्पिः पयांसै च
lines_iast: saṃskṛtāni ca māṃsāni dadhi sarpiḥ payāṃsai ca

words.gram: m. nom. pl., dvandva of adjectives

hindi: ईख, शालि चावल, माष, गेहूँ, गुड़ से बने पदार्थ, स्निग्ध और मधुर बस्तियाँ और सदा तेल का अभ्यङ्ग,
english: sugarcane, śāli rice, māṣa, wheat, preparations of jaggery (guḍa), unctuous and sweet enemas (basti), and oil massage (abhyaṅga) at all times,
notes: The list of nourishing measures runs from 29 to 33 (one sentence); the verb ādhatte and the result come in 33. māṣa: Vigna mungo (black gram), standard. sarvadā may go with the oil massage only or with the whole line.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: स्निग्ध उद्वर्तन, स्नान, गन्ध और माला का सेवन, श्वेत वस्त्र, समय पर दोषों का निकालना,
english: unctuous rubbing (udvartana), bathing, the use of perfumes and garlands, white clothing, the drawing out of the doṣas at the proper time,
notes: The list of nourishing measures runs from 29 to 33 (one sentence); the verb ādhatte and the result come in 33. avasecana literally 'pouring off'; here the timely removal of the doṣas. yathākālam may also qualify the whole list.

hindi: और रसायन तथा वृष्य योगों का सेवन — यह सब अति कृशता को नष्ट करके मनुष्यों में शरीर का उत्तम उपचय उत्पन्न करता है।
english: and the use of rejuvenative (rasāyana) and aphrodisiac applications: this destroys excessive leanness and produces the greatest increase of body (upacaya) in men.
notes: End of the list begun in 29. The verb ādhatte is singular: the whole list is taken as one subject (or it agrees with the nearest item, upasevanam). rasāyanānām may be a noun ('of rejuvenatives') or an adjective with yogānām.

words.gram: n. gen. pl., gerundive (kṛtya) √kṛ used as noun

hindi: कार्यों की चिन्ता न करने से, सन्तर्पण से और निद्रा में आसक्ति से मनुष्य निश्चय ही सूअर के समान पुष्ट होता है।
english: From not worrying about tasks, from nourishing therapy (saṃtarpaṇa), and from indulgence in sleep a man certainly grows plump like a boar.

text_flags.why: Typing error: 'ṛ' (Devanagari कऋयाणां) cannot stand here; the sense 'of tasks', governed by acintanāt, needs kāryāṇām. Syllable count is the same.

notes: dhruvam 'certainly' may go with the whole sentence or with saṃtarpaṇena.

hindi: किन्तु जब मन के थक जाने पर क्लम से युक्त कर्मात्मा अपने विषयों से हट जाते हैं, तब मनुष्य सोता है।
english: But when the mind is exhausted, and the karmātmans (those whose nature is action), overcome by exhaustion (klama), withdraw from their objects, then a person sleeps.
notes: manasi klānte is a locative absolute. karmātmānaḥ is taken as a bahuvrīhi 'those whose self is action'; the noun it refers to (the organs) is not stated in the line, so the rendering is uncertain.
lines_deva: यदा तु मनसि क्लान्ते कर्मात्मानः क्लमान्विताः
lines_iast: yadā tu manasi klānte karmātmānaḥ klamānvitāḥ

hindi: सुख और दुःख, पुष्टि और कृशता, बल और अबल, पुरुषत्व और नपुंसकता, ज्ञान और अज्ञान, जीवन और उसका अभाव — ये निद्रा के अधीन हैं।
english: Happiness and misery, nourishment and leanness, strength and weakness, virility and impotence, knowledge and ignorance, life and its absence depend on sleep.
notes: jīvitaṃ na ca: literally 'life and not (life)'. nidrāyattam is printed with final m before s (निद्रायत्तम्) instead of anusvāra; a spelling matter, not flagged.
lines_deva: निद्रायत्तम् सुखं दुःखं पुष्टिः कार्श्यं बलाबलम्
वृषता क्लीबता ज्ञानमज्ञानं जीवितं न च
lines_iast: nidrāyattam sukhaṃ duḥkhaṃ puṣṭiḥ kārśyaṃ balābalam
vṛṣatā klībatā jñānamajñānaṃ jīvitaṃ na ca

hindi: असमय में, अत्यधिक, अथवा बिल्कुल न सेवन की गई निद्रा दूसरी कालरात्रि के समान सुख और आयु को हर लेती है।
english: Sleep indulged in at the wrong time, in excess, or not at all takes away happiness and life like another night of doom (kālarātri).
notes: na ca ... niṣevitā is read as 'and not indulged in at all', a third improper use beside the wrong time and excess. kālarātri: literally 'night of Kāla (time, death)'.

hindi: वही निद्रा उचित रूप से सेवन की जाने पर शरीर को सुख और आयु से युक्त करती है, जैसे आई हुई सत्य बुद्धि योगी पुरुष को सिद्धि से युक्त करती है।
english: That same sleep, properly used, on the other hand endows the body with happiness and life, as true insight (buddhi), once it has come, endows a yogin with accomplishment (siddhi).
notes: The verb yuṅkte serves both halves of the simile.
lines_deva: सैव युक्ता पुनर्युङ्क्ते निद्रा देहं सुखायुषा
lines_iast: saiva yuktā punaryuṅkte nidrā dehaṃ sukhāyuṣā

words.gloss: worn out by singing, study, wine, women, work, loads and travel
words.gram: m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: गायन, अध्ययन, मद्य, स्त्री, कर्म, भार उठाने और मार्ग चलने से क्षीण हुए लोग, अजीर्ण वाले, क्षत, क्षीण, वृद्ध, बालक तथा निर्बल,
english: Those worn out by singing, study, wine, women, work, carrying loads and travelling; those with indigestion, the wounded, the wasted, the old, children and likewise the weak;
notes: The list of those who may sleep by day runs from 39 to 41 (one sentence; verb severan in 41). karśita literally 'emaciated', here 'worn out'. tathābalāḥ is split tathā abalāḥ 'the weak'; abalā can also mean 'woman', but women are not the natural sense in a list of the weak.

words.gloss: afflicted by thirst, diarrhoea and pain
words.gram: m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

words.gloss: the fallen, the injured and the insane

hindi: प्यास, अतिसार और शूल से पीड़ित, श्वास के रोगी, हिक्का के रोगी, कृश, गिरे हुए, चोट खाए हुए, उन्मत्त, सवारी और जागरण से थके हुए,
english: those afflicted by thirst, diarrhoea (atīsāra) and pain (śūla); those with dyspnoea (śvāsa), those with hiccup (hikkā), the lean; those who have fallen, the injured, the insane; those exhausted by riding and by keeping awake;
notes: Continues the list of 39 to 41. atīsāra is printed with long ī (a common spelling of atisāra); not flagged.

words.gloss: exhausted by anger, grief and fear
words.gram: m. nom. pl., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: क्रोध, शोक और भय से थके हुए और जो दिन में सोने के अभ्यस्त हैं — ये सब सभी ऋतुओं में दिन में सो सकते हैं।
english: those exhausted by anger, grief and fear, and those who are accustomed to day-sleep: all these may take day-sleep in every season.

text_flags.why: Possible typing error: severan needs an object, and sārvakālikam (m. acc. sg.) points to an accusative divāsvapnam; the printed divāsvapnā (m. nom. pl.) has no clear construction. Syllable count is the same.

notes: End of the list begun in 39. sarva = sarve before e (e + vowel). sārvakālikam 'belonging to all times'; taken as 'in every season' because 43 and 44 contrast Grīṣma with the other seasons.

hindi: क्योंकि इस प्रकार इनमें धातुओं की समता और बल उत्पन्न होता है, श्लेष्मा अङ्गों को पुष्ट करता है और आयु की स्थिरता होती है।
english: For in this way balance of the dhātus and strength arise in them; Kapha (śleṣman) nourishes the limbs, and there is stability of life.
lines_deva: श्लेष्मा पुष्णाति चाङ्गानि स्थैर्यं भवति चायुषः
lines_iast: śleṣmā puṣṇāti cāṅgāni sthairyaṃ bhavati cāyuṣaḥ

hindi: किन्तु ग्रीष्म में, आदान से रूक्ष हुए लोगों के लिए, मारुत के बढ़ने पर और रातों के अत्यन्त छोटे होने के कारण दिन में सोना प्रशस्त है।
english: But in Grīṣma, for those made dry by ādāna (taking up), when Vāta (māruta) is increasing and because the nights are very short, day-sleep is commended.

text_flags.why: Possible typing error: 'atisaṃkṣipā' cannot be parsed; the sense 'because of the extreme shortness of the nights' (with rātrīṇām) needs an ablative of cause, atisaṃkṣepāt, whose final t before d gives ddi-. Syllable count is the same.

notes: Grīṣma: the hot season (summer). vardhamāne mārute is a locative absolute. The split of the second line rests on the suggested correction.

words.gloss: other than Grīṣma (lit. with Grīṣma excluded)

hindi: ग्रीष्म को छोड़कर अन्य ऋतुओं में दिन में सोने से श्लेष्मा और पित्त कुपित होते हैं; इसलिए उन ऋतुओं में दिन में सोना प्रशस्त नहीं है।
english: In the seasons other than Grīṣma, Kapha (śleṣman) and Pitta become aggravated by day-sleep; therefore day-sleep is not commended in them.

hindi: मेदस्वी, सदा स्नेह का सेवन करने वाले, कफ-प्रधान, कफ के रोगों वाले और दूषीविष से पीड़ित लोग कभी भी दिन में न सोएँ।
english: The fat, those who constantly take fat (sneha), the Kapha-predominant, those with Kapha diseases, and those afflicted by dūṣīviṣa (vitiating poison) should never sleep by day.

text_flags.why: Word-division error: the 'a' of ca has been printed at the head of the next word (दूषीविषार्ताश्च् अदिवा); the words are ca divā. Syllable count is the same.

notes: dūṣīviṣa: literally 'vitiating poison'; kept as a term.

hindi: हलीमक, सिर का शूल, स्तैमित्य, अङ्गों का भारीपन, अङ्गमर्द, अग्नि का नाश और हृदय का प्रलेप,
english: halīmaka, pain in the head (śiraḥśūla), staimitya (torpor), heaviness of the limbs, body-ache (aṅgamarda), loss of the digestive fire (agni), a coating of the heart (hṛdaya),
notes: The list of the ill effects of unwholesome day-sleep runs from 46 to 49 (verb bhavet in 49). halīmaka is kept as a disease name.

words.gloss: swelling, loss of taste, nausea, pīnasa and ardhāvabhedaka

hindi: शोफ, अरोचक, हृल्लास, पीनस, अर्धावभेदक, कोठ, अरुस्, पिडकाएँ, कण्डू, तन्द्रा, कास, गले के रोग,
english: swelling (śopha), loss of taste (arocaka), nausea (hṛllāsa), pīnasa, ardhāvabhedaka, koṭha, sores (arus), eruptions (piḍakā), itching (kaṇḍū), drowsiness (tandrā), cough (kāsa), diseases of the throat,
notes: Continues the list of 46 to 49. koṭhāruḥpiḍakāḥ is read koṭha + arus (n., 'sore'; visarga in compound before p) + piḍakāḥ; a dvandva takes the gender of its last member. koṭha is kept as a term.

words.gram: m. nom. sg., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

words.gloss: setting in motion the course of poison

hindi: स्मृति और बुद्धि का मोह, स्रोतों का अवरोध, ज्वर, इन्द्रियों की असमर्थता और विष के वेग का प्रवर्तन —
english: confusion of memory and intellect, obstruction of the channels (srotas), fever (jvara), incapacity of the senses, and the setting in motion of the course (vega) of poison
notes: Continues the list of 46 to 49. vega of poison: its course or onset, not an urge.

words.gram: m. acc. sg., dvandva of adjectives, agreeing with svapnam

hindi: ये दिन में अहितकर सोने के सेवन से मनुष्यों में होते हैं; इसलिए बुद्धिमान व्यक्ति हितकर और अहितकर निद्रा को जानकर सुखपूर्वक सोए।
english: These arise in men from indulging in unwholesome day-sleep; therefore the wise man, having understood sleep as wholesome and unwholesome, should sleep happily.
notes: End of the list begun in 46; the singular bhavet takes the whole list as subject. hitāhitam is read as an adjective dvandva agreeing with svapnam; a neuter samāhāra 'the wholesome and the unwholesome' is possible but leaves svapnam unconstrued. divāsvapna is day-sleep, not dreaming.
lines_deva: तस्माद्धिताहितं स्वप्नं बुद्ध्वा स्वप्यात् सुखं बुधः
lines_iast: tasmāddhitāhitaṃ svapnaṃ buddhvā svapyāt sukhaṃ budhaḥ

hindi: रात में जागना रूक्ष है, दिन में सोना स्निग्ध है, परन्तु बैठे-बैठे ऊँघना न रूक्ष है और न स्रोतों को अवरुद्ध करने वाला।
english: Waking at night is drying (rūkṣa); sleeping by day is unctuous (snigdha); but dozing while seated is neither drying nor channel-clogging.

text_flags.why: Typing error: there is no word jāgarāṇa; the sense 'waking' (opposed to prasvapanam) needs jāgaraṇam. Syllable count is the same.

notes: pracalāyita: ppp. of the denominative pracalāya- 'to nod, doze', used as a noun.
lines_deva: रात्रौ जागराणं रूक्षं स्निग्धं प्रस्वपनं दिवा
lines_iast: rātrau jāgarāṇaṃ rūkṣaṃ snigdhaṃ prasvapanaṃ divā

words.gloss: in the maintenance of the body

words.gram: n. nom. du., tat-puruṣa (dvandva first member)

hindi: शरीर के धारण में जैसे आहार है, वैसे ही निद्रा सुखकर मानी गई है; और स्थूलता तथा कृशता विशेष रूप से निद्रा और आहार से उत्पन्न होती हैं।
english: As food is in the maintenance of the body, so sleep is held to be conducive to well-being; and obesity and leanness arise especially from sleep and food.

text_flags.why: Typing error: 'smutthe' has lost an 'a'; samuttha 'arising from' is needed, and the half-line is one syllable short without it (स्वप्नाहारस्मुत्थे द = 7 syllables).
Typing error (द for च): the sense needs ca 'and', and it restores the 8th syllable.

words.gloss: oil massage and rubbing with unguents
of domestic, marsh and aquatic animals
words.gram: m. nom. pl., dvandva of adjectives

hindi: अभ्यङ्ग और उत्सादन, स्नान, ग्राम्य, आनूप और औदक प्राणियों के मांसरस, दही के साथ शालि चावल का भोजन, दूध, स्नेह, मद्य, मन का सुख,
english: Oil massage (abhyaṅga) and rubbing with unguents (utsādana), bathing, the meat-juices (rasa) of domestic, marsh (ānūpa) and aquatic (audaka) animals, a meal of śāli rice with curd, milk, fat (sneha), wine, ease of mind,
notes: The list of what brings on sleep runs from 52 to 54 (verb ānayanti in 54). rasa with these animal adjectives is taken as meat-juice. sadadhi may also go with kṣīram ('milk with curd').
lines_deva: शाल्यन्नं सदधि क्षीरं स्नेहो मद्यं मनःसुखम्
lines_iast: śālyannaṃ sadadhi kṣīraṃ sneho madyaṃ manaḥsukham

hindi: मन के अनुकूल गन्ध और शब्द, संवाहन, नेत्रों का तर्पण, सिर और मुख पर लेप,
english: smells and sounds agreeable to the mind, massages (saṃvāhana), tarpaṇa of the eyes, a paste (lepa) on the head and face,
notes: Continues the list of 52 to 54. manaso 'nuguṇāḥ qualifies both gandhāḥ and śabdāḥ.

hindi: भली-भाँति बिछी हुई शय्या, सुखकर घर और अभ्यस्त समय — ये किसी कारण से नष्ट हुई निद्रा को शीघ्र ले आते हैं।
english: a well-spread bed, a comfortable house and the accustomed time: these quickly bring on sleep that has been lost through some cause.

text_flags.why: Possible typing error: the feminine svāstīrṇā has no feminine noun to agree with; śayanam is neuter, so svāstīrṇam is expected. Syllable count is the same.

Possible typing error: the printed short final a leaves the participle without agreement. Lengthening gives pranaṣṭā (f. nom. sg.), agreeing with yā: a clean relative clause 'sleep, which is lost through a cause'. Syllable count unchanged.

notes: End of the list begun in 52. 'pranaṣṭā yā nimittataḥ' is a relative clause: 'which (sleep) is lost through a cause'. sukham may also go with kālaḥ only if read as an adverb; taken with veśma.

hindi: शरीर और सिर का विरेक, छर्दन, भय, चिन्ता, क्रोध, तथा धूम, व्यायाम, रक्तमोक्षण,
english: Evacuation (vireka) of the body and of the head, emesis (chardana), fear, worry, anger, likewise medicated smoking (dhūma), exercise, bloodletting,
notes: The list of what checks excessive sleep runs from 55 to 56 (verb vārayanti in 56); 57 adds that these are also causes of loss of sleep.

hindi: उपवास, असुखकर शय्या, मन की उदारता और तम पर विजय — ये उत्पन्न हुई अहितकर अतिनिद्रा को रोकते हैं।
english: fasting, an uncomfortable bed, nobility of mind (sattva) and the conquest of tamas: these check unwholesome excessive sleep that has arisen.
notes: End of the list begun in 55. nidrāprasaṅga: 'attachment to sleep', i.e. excessive sleep.

words.gram: n. nom. sg., gerundive (kṛtya) √kṛ used as noun

hindi: ये ही निद्रा-नाश के कारण जानने चाहिए, तथा कार्य, काल, विकार, प्रकृति और वायु।
english: These same are to be known as the causes of loss of sleep, and also work, time (kāla), disorder (vikāra), nature (prakṛti) and Vāta (vāyu).
notes: eta = ete before a vowel (e + vowel). kāla may mean time of life (age) or season; prakṛti may mean the person's constitution; both left literal.
lines_deva: एत एव च विज्ञेया निद्रानाशस्य हेतवः
lines_iast: eta eva ca vijñeyā nidrānāśasya hetavaḥ

words.gloss: arising from fatigue of mind and body
words.gram: f. nom. sg., bahuvrīhi (dvandva first member)

words.gloss: arising from the nature of night

hindi: निद्रा तम से उत्पन्न, श्लेष्मा से उत्पन्न, मन और शरीर के श्रम से उत्पन्न, आगन्तुकी, व्याधि का अनुसरण करने वाली और रात्रि के स्वभाव से उत्पन्न होती है।
english: Sleep is born of tamas, arises from Kapha (śleṣman), arises from fatigue of the mind and the body, is exogenous (āgantukī), follows a disease, and arises from the nature of night.
notes: Upajāti metre (11 syllables a quarter). The line does not state a number of kinds: manaḥśarīraśramasaṃbhavā may name one kind or two (from mental and from bodily fatigue). āgantukī is printed as a separate feminine adjective in one token with vyādhyanuvartinī; it could also be read as qualifying it ('following an exogenous disease'), but the feminine ending favours a separate kind. Verbless sentence.

words.gloss: arising from the nature of night

hindi: जो रात्रि के स्वभाव से उत्पन्न मानी गई है, उसे उसके जानकार भूतधात्री कहते हैं; तम से उत्पन्न को पाप का मूल कहते हैं; और शेष को वे व्याधियों में गिनाते हैं।
english: The sleep that is held to arise from the nature of night, those who know it call the nurse of beings (bhūtadhātrī); the one born of tamas they call the root of evil (agha); the rest, again, they assign to diseases.
notes: Upajāti metre. śeṣāḥ is taken as f. acc. pl. (the remaining kinds of sleep), object of nirdiśanti; the subject is the same experts.
lines_deva: रात्रिस्वभावप्रभवा मता या तां भूतधात्रीं प्रवदन्ति तज्ज्ञाः
lines_iast: rātrisvabhāvaprabhavā matā yā tāṃ bhūtadhātrīṃ pravadanti tajjñāḥ

hindi: यहाँ श्लोक हैं: निन्दित पुरुष, उनमें से जो दो विशेष रूप से निन्दित हैं, निन्दा का कारण, उन दोनों के दोष, निन्दितों की चिकित्सा,
english: Here, the verses: the censured persons; the two among them who are especially censured; the cause of their censure; the faults (doṣa) of those two; the treatment of the censured;
notes: Lead-in 'tatra ślokāḥ' kept as line a as the edition groups it. The summary runs to 62 (verb vyājahāra). doṣāḥ here means the faults or ill effects of the two; it may also be read as the doṣas involved. tayoḥ may go with doṣāḥ or with ninditabheṣajam.

words.gloss: for one who sleeps too much
for one who does not sleep

hindi: किनके लिए कब निद्रा हितकर है और किनके लिए कब अहितकर, अतिनिद्रा वाले और निद्रारहित के लिए औषध, और वह किससे उत्पन्न होती है,
english: for whom and when sleep is wholesome, and for whom and when it is unwholesome; the medicine for one who sleeps too much and for one who does not sleep; and from what it arises;
notes: Continues the summary of 60 to 62. atinidrāya and anidrāya are datives of bahuvrīhis (atinidra, anidra) naming persons; the feminine nidrā would give -nidrāyai.
lines_deva: येभ्यो यदा हिता निद्रा येभ्यश्चाप्यहिता यदा
lines_iast: yebhyo yadā hitā nidrā yebhyaścāpyahitā yadā

words.gloss: in (the chapter) enumerating the eight censured

hindi: और जो-जो निद्रा जैसे प्रभाव वाली है — यह सब अत्रिज पुनर्वसु ने आठ निन्दितों की गणना वाले (अध्याय) में कहा।
english: and what each kind of sleep is and what effect it has: all this the Atri-born Punarvasu declared in the chapter that enumerates the eight censured (persons).

text_flags.why: Typing error: the word must be f. nom. sg. nidrā, agreeing with yā yā and yathāprabhāvā.
Typing error: dental t after ṣ (अष्ता) should be retroflex ṭ (ṣṭ), and 'āu' (ताउ) is the diphthong au of aṣṭau 'eight'; the colophon of this chapter spells aṣṭau-.
Typing error: doubled vowel (हाअर); the perfect is vyājahāra, and the extra a would add a syllable to the half-line.

notes: End of the summary begun in 60. aṣṭauninditasaṃkhyāte names this chapter by its subject (compare the colophon Aṣṭauninditīya).
lines_deva: या या यथाप्रभावा च निद्र तत् सर्वमत्रिजः
lines_iast: yā yā yathāprabhāvā ca nidra tat sarvamatrijaḥ

hindi: इस प्रकार अग्निवेश द्वारा रचित और चरक द्वारा प्रतिसंस्कृत तन्त्र के श्लोकस्थान में अष्टौनिन्दितीय नामक इक्कीसवाँ अध्याय।
english: Thus, in the Śloka section (Ślokasthāna) of the treatise composed by Agniveśa and redacted by Caraka, the twenty-first chapter, named Aṣṭauninditīya.
notes: Chapter colophon; the Sanskrit has no verb and the translation keeps it verbless. The title is a derived word in -īya, not split.
